colophon: Thus ends the Sri Narasimha Kavacham, spoken by Prahlada, in the Brahmanda Purana.

lines.1: I shall tell the Narasimha armor, spoken long ago by Prahlada:
lines.2: holy, giving every protection, destroying every affliction,
lines.3: bringing every prosperity, granting heaven and liberation.
lines.4: Meditate on Narasimha, lord of the gods, seated on a golden lion throne,
lines.5: mouth open wide, three-eyed, radiant as the autumn moon,
lines.6: his left side embraced by Lakshmi, attended by his divine powers,
lines.7: four-armed, soft of limb, shining with golden earrings,
lines.8: his chest graced with lotuses, his arms bound with jeweled armlets,
lines.9: gleaming like molten gold, dressed in spotless yellow,
lines.10: with the flashing radiance of the rubies in the crowns of Indra and the other gods
lines.11: making his two feet shine; bearing conch, discus, and his other weapons,
lines.12: joyful, praised with reverence by Garuda.
lines.13: Seating him in the lotus of one's own heart, one should recite the armor:
lines.14: may Narasimha, who came forth to protect the worlds, protect my head.
lines.15: May he who, though everywhere, dwelt in the pillar, protect my forehead and my voice;
lines.16: may Narasimha, whose eyes are moon, sun, and fire, protect my eyes.
lines.17: May the Man Lion, fond of the praises of great sages, protect my memory;
lines.18: may the lion-nosed one guard my nose, and he who loves Lakshmi's face, my mouth.
lines.19: May Narasimha, master of all knowledge, protect my tongue;
lines.20: may the moon-faced one, ever revered by Prahlada, protect my face.
lines.21: May Narasimha protect my throat; he who ends the earth's burden, my shoulders;
lines.22: may Narasimha, his arms shining with divine weapons, protect my arms.
lines.23: May Narasimha, giver of boons to the gods, protect my hands on every side;
lines.24: may Hari, whom yogis reach, protect my heart and my dwelling.
lines.25: May he who tore open the chest and belly of Hiranyaksha protect my waist;
lines.26: may the Man Lion, praised by Brahma who rose from his own navel, protect my navel.
lines.27: May he on whose hips rest millions of universes protect my hips;
lines.28: may he who sees the hidden form of the most secret mantras protect my secret parts.
lines.29: May he who is born in the mind protect my thighs; he who took a man's form, my knees;
lines.30: may the Man Lion, who lifts the burden of the earth, protect my shins.
lines.31: May Narahari the lord, giver of heaven's kingdom to the gods, protect my feet;
lines.32: may the thousand-headed Person protect my body in every part.
lines.33: May the most fierce one protect me from the east; the eldest of great heroes, from the southeast;
lines.34: Mahavishnu in the south, and the great blaze in the southwest;
lines.35: in the west may the lord of all protect me, and in every direction he whose faces are everywhere;
lines.36: may Narasimha protect me in the northwest; he of terrifying form, in the north;
lines.37: in the northeast may the gracious one protect me, giver of every blessing;
lines.38: may the Man Lion, the death of death, protect me from the fear of worldly existence.
lines.39: This Narasimha armor, adorned by coming from Prahlada's mouth:
lines.40: the devotee who recites it daily is freed from all sins.
lines.41: In this world he is blessed with sons and wealth, and lives long;
lines.42: whatever desire he desires, that he attains, without doubt.
lines.43: He wins everywhere, and is victorious everywhere.
lines.44: It wards off the seizing powers of earth, mid-air, and heaven,
lines.45: is the supreme remover of the poison of scorpions and snakes,
lines.46: and the means of driving brahma-rakshasas and yakshas far away.
lines.47: This auspicious armor, written on birch bark or on a palm leaf
lines.48: and worn at the wrist: for the one who wears it, every undertaking succeeds.
lines.49: Among gods, demons, and humans alike, he wins his own victory,
lines.50: the disciplined person who recites it once a day, or at all three junctions of the day.
lines.51: He gains the blessing of all blessings, both enjoyment and liberation.
lines.52: For the pure-hearted who recite it thirty-two thousand times,
lines.53: the power of this armor-mantra comes to perfection.
lines.54: Charging sacred ash with this king of mantras,
lines.55: whoever marks the brow with it is freed from fear of the seizing planets.
lines.56: Chanting it three times over water given to them,
lines.57: whoever has it drunk, reciting the mantra and meditating on Narasimha:
lines.58: that person's diseases perish, even those that arise in the belly.
lines.59: Why say more? He becomes like Narasimha himself;
lines.60: whatever he holds in his mind, he attains, without doubt.
lines.61: Roaring, making others roar, flexing his mass of arms, striking with force,
lines.62: blazing, scorching, flinging and scattering the sons of Diti in heaven and on earth,
lines.63: bellowing, raging, ever destroying and ever sustaining in every direction,
lines.64: gazing, whirling hundreds of volleys of arrows: to the divine Lion I bow.
